name: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge

fee.note: Not confirmed. The refuge says to pay the entrance fee on Recreation.gov but doesn't publish the amount on the page I can reach — its own fees page returns a 404. Bring a card and expect to pay something.

birding.why: A twelve-mile drive through managed pools, salt marsh and mudflat, most of which you can bird without getting out of the car.
birding.scopeNote: Open water and mudflat at distance. A scope changes what this place is; binoculars alone leave a lot of gray dots.
birding.fromCarNote: The wildlife drive is the refuge. One of the rare Delaware outings that works better from the car — the vehicle is the blind, and stepping out is what puts birds up.

closures.what: All roads and trails closed. The visitor center stays open.
closures.why: Refuge hunt days. Three specific dates, published by the refuge — the kind of thing that ruins a two-hour drive and appears on no tourism page.

warnings: Salt marsh in summer means biting insects. May is the reason to come; repellent is the reason the trip stays pleasant.
The three 2026 hunt dates close every road and trail. Check them before driving from out of state.

sources.label: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge — U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service
sources.note: Read 9 August 2026. Publishes the 2026 hunting closure dates and directs fee payment to Recreation.gov without naming an amount.

outstanding: The entrance fee. Their own fees page 404s and the overview names no amount.
Restrooms — where, and whether they're open before the visitor center.
Observation towers: how many, where, and whether any is step-free.
How long the twelve-mile drive actually takes at birding pace.

name: Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge

fee.note: Not confirmed. Nothing published on the pages I can reach names a fee.

birding.why: Marsh, and 7.5 miles of trails — but a lot of the best of it is birded from the county roads crossing the marsh rather than from any trailhead.
birding.scopeNote: Marsh at distance rewards one. Not essential on the wooded trails.
birding.fromCarNote: The roads across the marsh are part of the refuge, and a first-timer who parks at a trailhead and walks can miss what they came for.

closures.when: Through the nesting season, reopening 1 October 2026
closures.why: Federally threatened piping plovers and state-endangered least terns nesting. The refuge's own closure, not a guess.
Heavily silted. The refuge says not to attempt it and to go west from Foord's Landing only.

birding.sensitiveNote: Piping plover and least tern nesting. The refuge closes Fowler Beach for it, and this page publishes the closure rather than anything that would help somebody get closer.

warnings: Fowler Beach is shut for nesting until 1 October 2026.
Don't take a canoe east on the canoe trail — the refuge says it's silted in.

sources.label: Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge — U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service
sources.note: Read 9 August 2026. Publishes the 7.5 miles of trails, the Fowler Beach nesting closure with its 1 October reopening, and the canoe-trail silting.

outstanding: Which county roads across the marsh are the productive ones, and where it's safe to stop a car.
